page: Amazon Web Services c8i.96xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the Nitro hypervisor architecture. It features two dedicated Intel Xeon 6975P-C processors with an x86_64 architecture, providing 192 physical cores and 384 vCPUs running at 3.9 GHz. The memory subsystem consists of 768.0 GB of DDR5 RAM rated at 7 GHz, delivering a compute-centric 2:1 vCPU-to-memory ratio (2.0 GB per core). Cache resources include a massive 480 MB L3 cache, complemented by 2 MB of L2 cache and 48 KB of L1d cache. Network connectivity provides a baseline bandwidth of 100 Gbps. The instance does not include integrated local storage or hardware GPUs.

Benchmark results demonstrate exceptional multi-threaded computational capabilities, ranking in the top 10% for multi-core stress-ng tests, PassMark CPU evaluation, Clang compilation, ray tracing, and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression. The CPU instruction set features AMX and AVX-512 vector extensions, driving high-tier results in extended instruction testing and hardware-accelerated encryption. Memory bandwidth tests indicate sustained large-block read throughput of 1,147.58 GB/sec and write throughput of 507.23 GB/sec, supporting high-rate Redis SET operations (509.89 million ops/sec) and static web serving throughput reaching 198.62 GB/sec. Conversely, single-threaded metrics such as single-core stress-ng perform in the median range.

Tradeoffs center around storage topology and sequential token generation constraints. Without bundled local NVMe storage, persistent data architectures rely entirely on network-attached storage or high-throughput external volumes across the 100 Gbps network fabric. For machine learning tasks, prompt processing performs at high tiers via Intel AMX matrix capabilities, but token generation speeds fall into lower performance bands due to the absence of dedicated GPU accelerators. The platform offers efficient resource consolidation for massive parallel compute pipelines, enterprise Clang compilation suites, high-concurrency microservice fleets, and in-memory key-value stores.
description: Amazon Web Services c8i.96xlarge is a high-density, compute-optimized instance powered by dedicated Intel Xeon 6975P-C processors on the Nitro hypervisor. The x86_64 configuration provides 192 physical cores, 384 vCPUs clocked at 3.9 GHz, 480 MB of L3 cache, and 768.0 GB of DDR5 memory running at 7 GHz. It includes baseline 100 Gbps network connectivity, without bundled local storage or GPUs. Benchmark evaluations show top-tier multi-threaded processing, leading PassMark CPU scores, advanced matrix instruction processing, and rapid uncached memory throughput exceeding 1,147 GB/sec for reads. Single-core throughput and sequential LLM token generation represent the architectural tradeoffs. This instance is suited for parallel batch processing, massive Clang software builds, distributed caching, and compute-heavy containerized workloads requiring high network bandwidth.
